section_summary: This section of a report surveys Japan’s economic recovery in 1948, including production, inflation, wages and living standards. It argues that trade deficits, depleted assets and natural resources, and reliance on foreign aid threaten that recovery. It then examines the problems economic stabilization may bring, including weak purchasing power, pressure on farmers and small enterprises, unemployment, and renewed inflation.

people.name: Douglas MacArthur

subfiles.title: Report on Japanese economic conditions and stabilization
subfiles.about: An analysis of Japan’s 1948 economic performance and the obstacles to stabilization, reconstruction and self-support.
subfiles.summary: The report records rising industrial and agricultural production, slower inflation and higher real wages, while warning that a large import surplus and foreign assistance sustain these gains. It describes inadequate depreciation, subsidies, deteriorating land and infrastructure, and living standards far below prewar levels. It anticipates that a single exchange rate and the Nine Economic Objectives will expose weak demand, strain farmers and small enterprises, and require changes to price controls. The final pages weigh fiscal restraint against the investment needed for reconstruction and begin a concluding call for gradual normalization of the economy.
